_comment: Directional power model for datacenter GPU/accelerator training, used to estimate the energy (kWh) of a training run so it can be placed in a greener region and/or timed to the cleanest hours. tdp_watts are PUBLISHED peak board power (TDP) from NVIDIA datasheets and corroborating sources; a training run does NOT sit at TDP the whole time, so energy = tdp_watts * gpu_count * default_utilization * hours, plus a per-GPU host overhead, all x datacenter PUE at calc time. ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE, directional estimates. NOT measured for your model/run. Replace with measured power telemetry before any non-directional use.
_sources: NVIDIA datasheets/product pages (A100 400W SXM; H100 700W SXM / 350W PCIe; H200 700W; T4 70W; L4 72W; V100 300W SXM; L40S 350W; B200 ~1000W; GB200 superchip ~1200W). Corroborated across NVIDIA, thundercompute, cyfuture, semianalysis, gmicloud (2024-2026). Values rounded.

_method.formula: energy_kwh = (sum over GPUs of [tdp_watts * utilization + host_overhead_watts_per_gpu]) / 1000 * gpu_hours_per_gpu * pue
_method.utilization_note: TDP is PEAK board power. Sustained training typically averages below TDP; default_utilization (0.85) is a documented directional assumption, overridable per call.
_method.host_overhead_note: Each accelerator is fed by host CPU/RAM/NIC/storage; host_overhead_watts_per_gpu is a rough per-GPU allocation of that non-GPU server draw. Directional.
_method.pue_note: Datacenter overhead multiplier taken from power.json pue_default at calculation time (not duplicated here).

gb200.name: NVIDIA GB200 Superchip
gb200._note: Two Blackwell GPUs + Grace CPU; TDP is the combined superchip.
